postMessage origin check uses substring match

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured Discourse URL. With `discourseUrl = "http://discourse.example.com/"`, messages from `http://discourse.example.co`, `http://discourse.example.c`, or even `http://d` pass the check, since all are substrings. true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Stored XSS: unescaped URL interpolated into raw_html post footer `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the article HTML without any escaping, and the resulting post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `cooked == raw` and no sanitization ever runs. The `url` is attacker-influenced: `EmbedController#best` accepts an arbitrary `embed_url` query param, and `TopicRetriever` only checks that its host equals `embeddable_host` (path/query are unrestricted). A URL such as `http:///real-post.html?x='onmouseover='alert(1)'` is a valid URI, is fetched successfully (most servers ignore the query string), and produces `href='...?x='onmouseover='alert(1)''`, which Nokogiri re-serializes as a live `onmouseover` attribute. Since the Referer check can be satisfied with a forged header from curl, an unauthenticated attacker can create a topic (authored by the configured embed user, typically staff) containing arbitrary JavaScript that executes on the forum's origin. The URL must be HTML-attribute-escaped (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) and ideally the footer should be built with a sanitizer.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` typo only works by accident

The header conditional is closed with `end if` instead of `end`. Ruby treats the trailing `if` as a modifier whose condition is the *next* compiled statement (the output-buffer append generated by ERB for the following whitespace/link), so the template happens to compile and the buffer call still runs before the branch. Any change to the following line (e.g. removing the blank lines or the logo link) can turn this into a syntax error or silently swallow the header. No spec renders this view (controller specs run without `render_views`), so the typo is not caught. Change to `<%- end %>` and add a rendering test.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds, crashing the whole poll

`poll_feed` calls `i.content.scrub` on every item. SimpleRSS only populates `content` from an Atom `<content>` element; RSS 2.0 feeds expose the body as `description` or `content:encoded` (accessed as `content_encoded`), so `i.content` is `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the loop is not protected, one such item aborts the entire hourly job (`retry: false`), so no items from a standard WordPress/Blogger-style RSS feed are ever imported. Fall back to `content_encoded`/`description` and skip items with no body.

postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Already-shipped migration modified to add force: true

This migration predates the PR and has already been applied on existing installs; editing it has no effect there but changes what new installs run. `force: true` makes `create_table` drop any existing `top_topics` table silently, so if the migration is re-run (e.g. after a manual rollback/replay or on a database where the table was created by `db:schema:load`) all top-topic data is destroyed without warning. Shipped migrations should not be edited; if a drop-if-exists is really needed for the test database, fix the test setup instead.

Deleted imported post/topic leaves a dangling TopicEmbed that crashes updates and permanently breaks the embed

`TopicEmbed` has no cleanup when its post or topic is deleted. `belongs_to :post` honours `Post`'s trashable default scope, so after a staff member deletes the imported topic `embed.post` is `nil`; the next feed poll with changed content calls `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!`, raising `NoMethodError` and aborting the job. Meanwhile `topic_id_for_embed` still returns the deleted topic id, so `EmbedController#best` builds a `TopicView` on a deleted topic (404) instead of falling through to re-import, and because the unique `embed_url` row persists the URL can never be imported again. Handle a missing post (treat as no embed / destroy the row) and remove TopicEmbed rows when the post or topic is destroyed.

Disqus importer silently drops --category support and original topic dates, and aborts on fetch failures

The `--category` option is removed and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` replaces the old `PostCreator` call that passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and `category: category_id`. Imported topics are now created in the default category with the import time instead of the original thread date, changing the behaviour of an existing CLI without mention. In addition `import_remote` performs `open(t[:link]).read` with no rescue, so a single dead link or `nil` link in the Disqus export (common for deleted pages) raises `OpenURI::HTTPError`/`TypeError` and aborts the entire import midway, after `RateLimiter.disable` and blacklist changes have already been applied (restored by `ensure`, but the import is left partial).

Import pipeline is subject to per-user rate limits and new-user host-spam detection

`PostCreator` is invoked with `skip_validations: true`, but that does not bypass `Post`'s `rate_limit` after_create hooks (`rate_limit_create_topic`/`rate_limit_create_post`, 1 per 5s, `max_topics_per_day: 20`) nor `rollback_if_host_spam_detected`. Unless the `embed_by_username` account is staff, importing a feed with more than one new item raises `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded` on the second topic and aborts the whole poll; a TL0 embed account also trips `newuser_spam_host_threshold` after three topics linking to the embeddable host (every import adds an `Imported from` link), causing posts to be rolled back and spam alerts sent to moderators. The Disqus importer in this same PR wraps its run in `RateLimiter.disable` precisely for this reason, but `PollFeed`/`TopicRetriever` do not. Either disable rate limiting around the import, pass an option to bypass it, or document that the embed user must be staff.

Outer transaction defeats PostCreator's post-commit job enqueueing and leaks side effects on unique-index collisions

`TopicEmbed.import` wraps `PostCreator#create` in `Topic.transaction`. `PostCreator` deliberately enqueues `process_post`/`feature_topic_users` and publishes MessageBus/TopicTrackingState events *after* its own transaction so workers don't see uncommitted rows (see the comment in `PostCreator#enqueue_jobs`). Nested inside the outer transaction those jobs are now enqueued before commit, so in production (`queue_jobs: true`) Sidekiq can pick up `process_post` for a post that is not yet visible or is later rolled back. The rollback case is real: the scheduled `PollFeed` and a `RetrieveTopic` job (which calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously) can import the same URL concurrently; both pass the `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).first` check, both create a topic+post, and the loser raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` from `TopicEmbed.create!`, which is unhandled, rolls back its topic, and leaves already-enqueued jobs, user stat updates and publishes referring to a vanished post. Create the TopicEmbed row inside PostCreator's transaction (or use an advisory lock / `find_or_create` with rescue) and keep job enqueueing after commit.

Rails 3 lockfile not updated for the new gems

The project dual-boots via `Gemfile.lock` (Rails 3, `RAILS3=1`) and `Gemfile_rails4.lock`. Only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` gains `ruby-readability`, `guess_html_encoding` and `simple-rss`. Booting in Rails 3 mode with `bundle install --deployment` / `--frozen` will fail because the Gemfile no longer matches its lockfile, and without frozen mode Bundler will re-resolve and rewrite the lockfile unexpectedly. Either update `Gemfile.lock` as well or drop the Rails 3 boot path.

Templates, feed parsing and import paths are untested; existing spec names mismatch behaviour

The controller specs never render `best.html.erb` or `loading.html.erb` (rspec-rails controller specs stub rendering), and `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil, so the `@topic_view.posts`/`topic.url` code and the `end if` typo are never exercised. `poll_feed_spec` only tests the guard conditions, not `poll_feed` itself (nil `content`, non-http links, CDATA handling). There are no tests for `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, URL escaping in the imported footer, or `absolutize_urls` with protocol-relative URLs. The spec at line 8 is titled "is 404 without an embed_url" but the request actually fails with 403 from `ensure_embeddable` (no host configured) and only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it does not test the `params.require` path at all.

Unauthenticated callers can mass-create topics and jobs via arbitrary embed_url values

Every request to `/embed/best` whose `embed_url` has no existing `TopicEmbed` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job. The only guard is a forgeable `Referer` host check, and the throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed on the *exact* URL string (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`), with no normalization of query strings, fragments, trailing slashes or scheme. An attacker can therefore request `http://<embeddable_host>/post?x=1`, `?x=2`, ... and each one (a) enqueues a Sidekiq job, (b) synchronously re-fetches and re-imports the entire RSS feed inside that job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), (c) performs an outbound HTTP GET + Readability parse, and (d) creates a new topic/post as the embed user because most servers return 200 for unknown query strings. The result is unbounded forum spam from a privileged account, unbounded outbound requests to the embeddable host and feed, and queue growth (the `RetrieveTopic` job does not set `retry: false`, so each 404/network failure is retried ~25 times). Additionally the loading page reloads every 30s forever when retrieval can never succeed. URLs should be canonicalized (strip query/fragment, enforce http(s) scheme), throttled globally as well as per URL, and ideally only URLs present in the feed should be importable.

Unconditional CGI.unescapeHTML turns entity-escaped text inside CDATA content into live HTML

SimpleRSS strips `<![CDATA[ ... ]]>` markers but does not HTML-unescape the contents, which is already literal HTML. Applying `CGI.unescapeHTML` to it decodes entities that are part of the HTML text itself: `<script>` shown in a code sample becomes a real `<script>` tag, `&` becomes a bare `&`, etc. Since the post is stored with `cook_method: raw_html` and never sanitized, escaped markup that the blog author intentionally displayed as text is executed/rendered as markup on the forum. The unescape should only be applied when the element was not CDATA-wrapped (or the content should be parsed with a real XML parser).

`String#scrub` requires Ruby 2.1; no polyfill is provided

`i.content.scrub` relies on `String#scrub`, which was introduced in Ruby 2.1.0 (released 25 Dec 2013). The Gemfile in this PR does not add a backport such as `string-scrub`, and nothing in the diff adds a freedom patch, so on the Ruby 2.0 installs the project supported at this time the poll job raises `NoMethodError` on the first item.

`open(url)` depends on open-uri being required by an unrelated file

`import_remote` calls `Kernel#open` with an http URL but `topic_embed.rb` never requires `open-uri`; the only `require 'open-uri'` in this PR is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. Whenever `TopicEmbed.import_remote` is reached without `Jobs::PollFeed` having been loaded first (e.g. the Disqus thor task or a dev-mode Sidekiq process with feed polling disabled), `open("http://...")` falls through to plain `File.open` and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Add `require 'open-uri'` to this file (and consider an explicit timeout on the request).

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative (//host/...) links and images

The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`, which are very common in blog/RSS HTML. `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes and the result is prefixed with the article host, producing `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png` — a broken link/image. The same happens for `img[src]` at line 70. Only rewrite when the value starts with a single `/` (i.e. not `//`), or resolve with `URI.join(url, href)`, which also handles the plain relative paths (`images/x.png`) that this code currently ignores.

embed.css and embed.js are not added to the asset precompile list

The PR adds `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and references them via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and as the script the third-party site must include, but `config/application.rb` (which maintains an explicit `config.assets.precompile` list in this app) is not changed. In production, where `config.assets.compile` is false, non-precompiled assets are not in the manifest: the stylesheet helper falls back to `/stylesheets/embed.css` (404, unstyled iframe) and `/assets/embed.js` requested by embedding sites 404s, so the feature does not work at all outside development. Add both files to `config.assets.precompile`.

embed_url is a 255-char varchar with a unique index; long URLs fail the import unhandled

`t.string :embed_url` creates a `varchar(255)` column. Blog permalinks with long slugs or query strings (the controller accepts any query string) can exceed 255 characters; the `TopicEmbed.create!` then raises `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` after the topic and post have been created, rolling the outer transaction back and failing the job each time the URL is requested. Use `text` (or validate length before fetching) and index accordingly. Also note `force: true` on `create_table` will silently drop a pre-existing `topic_embeds` table and its data if the migration is ever re-run.

raw_html cook method lets any later editor store unsanitized HTML

`Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`, and `before_save` recomputes `cooked = cook(raw, ...)` on every save. `cook_method` is persisted on the post, so any subsequent edit of an imported post through the normal `PostRevisor` path (e.g. a moderator editing it from the UI, or the embed account being compromised) stores whatever HTML/JS the editor types, bypassing the sanitizer and the `after_post_cook` plugin filter entirely. Moderators normally cannot post raw HTML; this gives them (and anyone who gains the embed user's credentials) a persistent XSS vector on the forum origin. Consider sanitizing raw_html output through the HTML whitelist, or resetting `cook_method` to regular when a post is edited by anyone other than the import pipeline.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`align-items` mixin emits a non-existent `-ms-align-items` property and passes values through unmapped to legacy syntaxes

`-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version ever implemented (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so line 121 is dead output in every compiled rule that uses the mixin. More importantly, the mixin passes `$alignment` verbatim into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, which only accept `start`/`end` rather than the modern `flex-start`/`flex-end`; likewise `order()` forwards `$val` into `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, which requires a positive integer (default 1) while modern `order` defaults to 0 and allows negatives. Today's call sites (`center`, `baseline`, `2`, `3`) happen to be valid in all syntaxes, but the mixins silently produce invalid legacy declarations for any other value, defeating their purpose. Either map values (`flex-start`→`start`, `$val + 1` for ordinal-group) or drop the legacy prefixes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

false_positives.candidate:
Header `.panel` right-alignment relies on `margin-left: auto`, which the 2009 `-webkit-box` fallback the mixins emit does not support

The new `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` so that legacy engines (Android 2.x–4.3 stock browser, Safari < 6.1, old Firefox) get a flex layout. However, the header now positions `.panel` on the right solely via `margin-left: auto` (replacing the previous `float: right`). In the 2009 box model, `auto` margins on box children are computed as zero, so in exactly those browsers the fallback is targeting, the panel (user/notification/search icons, login buttons) will collapse to sit immediately after the title/extra-info instead of at the right edge. Previously `float: right` worked everywhere. Either drop the legacy prefixes (so those browsers fall back to normal block flow) or add a 2009-compatible mechanism (e.g. `-webkit-box-pack: justify` on `.contents` or `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on the preceding item).

Making `.small-action` a flex container breaks right-alignment of its action buttons

`.small-action` is now `display: flex`, but `.small-action-desc` has no `flex: 1`/`flex-grow`, so it shrinks to its content width instead of filling the row as the old block did. The `.small-action button { float: right; }` rule (line 309) therefore either has no effect (if a button is a direct flex child, floats are ignored on flex items) or only floats to the right edge of the now content-sized `.small-action-desc`, placing the edit/delete buttons directly after a short description like "closed 2 hours ago" instead of at the right edge of the post. Add `flex: 1 1 auto` (or `width: 100%`) to `.small-action-desc`, or use `margin-left: auto` on the buttons.

PR title claims a performance optimization; description is a placeholder

The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and described as "Test 5". Nothing in the diff is a performance change: it is a layout refactor replacing float-based positioning of `.title`/`.panel`/`.extra-info-wrapper` and `.small-action` with flexbox, plus new vendor-prefix mixins, with visible rendering consequences (removed margins/paddings, new ordering). The misleading title and empty description will mislead anyone bisecting a header/small-action layout regression later and give reviewers no information about intended visual changes or browser support goals. The title and description should describe the actual change and the browsers the legacy prefixes are meant to support.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Placeholder string "refresh_token" is injected into parsed token data and persisted, overwriting real refresh tokens

When the parsed response lacks `refresh_token`, the function mutates the data to `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`. This runs in both the sync and non-sync branches. In the non-sync Office365 path, `refreshTokenResponseSchema` marks `refresh_token` optional; if Microsoft omits it, the spread `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` now replaces the stored, valid refresh token with the literal string, permanently breaking the credential (previously the spread left it untouched). true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`minimumTokenResponseSchema` computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]"; schema strips every field except access_token

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are computed property keys. Calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema object returns the literal string `"[object Object]"`, so both lines define the same key (the second wins) and the schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. There is no `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()`, so when credential sync is enabled every other field in the provider response (expires_in, expiry_date, refresh_token, scope, token_type, instance_url, ...) is silently stripped. Consequences: Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN (serialised as null), after which `zoomTokenSchema.parse` fails and Zoom breaks; Office365 never updates `expires_in` so the token is treated as expired and re-fetched on every call; Salesforce loses `instance_url`. The comment "Assume that any property with a number is the expiry" describes behaviour that is not implemented. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` (and an explicit expiry field) instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object on every token refresh

`parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)`, i.e. an object of the form `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, not the parsed credentials themselves. In `refreshAccessToken` the return value is assigned to `key` and written straight to the DB with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. The previous code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the plain credential object. The next time the service is constructed, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails because `access_token`/`refresh_token` are no longer top-level fields, so the Google Calendar integration becomes permanently broken for that user until they reconnect. The other call sites (Office365, Zoom, Salesforce) correctly use `.data`; this one must too.

Salesforce now hits the token endpoint on every service instantiation and ignores the refreshed token

`getClient` (called from the constructor) now unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` with the stored refresh token on every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction (every booking, update, delete), with no expiry check. jsforce already refreshes lazily on 401, so this adds a network round-trip and Salesforce API quota usage to every operation. true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid body or undecryptable payload produce unhandled exceptions (500) and decrypted keys are stored unvalidated

`appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` on a malformed body, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a wrong key, malformed ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext. None of these are caught (the handler is not wrapped in `defaultResponder`/try-catch), so the caller receives a generic 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message, and the self-hoster cannot distinguish a bad payload from a server fault. The decrypted `keys` value is also written to `credential.key` without any shape validation, so a sender bug (e.g. encrypting the wrong object) silently corrupts the user's credential and only surfaces later when the app's credential schema parse fails.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for the new webhook endpoint or the shared OAuth refresh helpers

The PR adds a new authenticated API route that writes third-party credentials into the DB and two shared helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that now sit in the token-refresh path of nine integrations, but ships no unit or integration tests (the PR description explicitly states tests were not added or run). Several of the defects in this change — the `[object Object]` schema key, the SafeParse wrapper being stored as the Google credential key, the missing `prisma` import in Salesforce, and the dirName-vs-slug lookup — would have been caught by even a minimal test exercising the webhook with a known slug and a test asserting the shape written to `prisma.credential.update` after a refresh.

Request to the credential-sync endpoint carries no authentication

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as a form body, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other authentication material. The endpoint is expected to return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user ids, so the self-hoster has no way (short of network allow-listing) to verify the request originates from their Cal.com instance; anyone who can reach the endpoint can harvest every user's third-party tokens by enumerating ids. The PR already defines `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` for the inbound direction; the outbound request should at minimum send the same secret header so the endpoint can authenticate it.

Webhook looks up `appStoreMetadata` by slug, but the map is keyed by app directory name

`appStoreMetadata` (from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by the app's directory name (`googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`, ...), not by its slug (`google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing it with `app.slug` only works for apps whose dir name happens to equal the slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, zoho-bigin, webex). For the main apps this PR targets the lookup returns undefined and the endpoint responds 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug" even though the slug is correct, so credentials can never be synced for them. Use `getAppFromSlug(slug)` from `@calcom/app-store/utils` (or search `Object.values(appStoreMetadata)` by `slug`) instead.

Webhook secret compared with `!==` rather than a constant-time comparison

The secret header is validated with a plain string inequality against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. String comparison short-circuits on the first mismatching byte, which leaks timing information that can be used to recover the secret byte-by-byte on a network-reachable endpoint. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers (as other webhook handlers in the codebase do) and reject when lengths differ.

Zoom refresh uses app identifier "zoomvideo" while the app slug (and webhook) use "zoom"

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the self-hoster's credential-sync endpoint, but the Zoom app's slug/appId everywhere else is `"zoom"` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` `appId: "zoom"`, and the inbound webhook resolves apps via `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })`). A self-hoster keying their endpoint by the slug they push through the webhook will not recognise `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token refresh fails in sync mode. Every other call site passes the real slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`, ...); this one should pass `"zoom"`.

`findFirst` by userId+appId overwrites an arbitrary credential for apps that allow multiple installs

Several apps (e.g. Google Calendar) allow a user to hold multiple credentials for the same `appId`. The webhook selects `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no ordering and updates whichever row comes back, so a sync for one connected account can clobber the keys of a different connected account of the same provider. There is also no uniqueness constraint, so two concurrent webhook calls for a new user/app pair can both take the `create` branch and produce duplicate credentials. The payload should identify the target credential (or the provider account) rather than relying on `findFirst`.

`prisma` is used but never imported in the Salesforce CalendarService

The new code in `getClient` calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but this file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` (the import list contains only jsforce, rrule, zod, CalEventParser, constants, http-error, logger, types, getAppKeysFromSlug and parseRefreshTokenResponse). This is a TypeScript compile error (`Cannot find name 'prisma'`) and, if it slipped through, a `ReferenceError` at runtime inside the constructor's promise, meaning every `SalesforceCalendarService` instantiation rejects and the Salesforce integration is completely non-functional.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn-context processes, so hung flusher processes are never killed

In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the PR wraps `process.kill()` in `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Production flusher processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which yields `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess` directly and is NOT a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`), so the check is always False for real processes and `kill()` is never invoked. The previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally and worked. Consequence: when a process is detected as hung ("hang" cause after `max-unhealthy-seconds`), the old process is left running while a replacement is spawned for the same shards. A slow-but-alive process will then flush the same shards concurrently with the new one (both can read the same expired segments from the Redis queue before `done_flush_segments` removes them, producing duplicate segments to Kafka), and up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS+1 processes can pile up per shard group. The same wrong check at line 346 in `join()` means `terminate()` is also never called on spawned processes (pre-existing, but this PR touched that code). Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` instead.

join() breaks out of the process loop on deadline, leaving remaining processes un-terminated

This pattern was harmless before because tagging was best-effort, but it now defeats the feature.

The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Device limit is only enforced for requests that volunteer the X-Grafana-Device-Id header

`TagDevice` returns nil immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Authenticate` then grants the anonymous identity. Because the header is entirely client-controlled, any client (scripts, curl, a browser with the header stripped) can use anonymous access without ever being counted or limited, so the new `device_limit` setting cannot be relied upon to cap anonymous usage. If the limit is meant to be an enforceable cap, requests without a device id should either be rejected when a limit is configured or be subject to a separate check; otherwise the limitation should be made explicit in the setting's documentation.

Device-limit tests cover only the rejection path, not the update-at-limit path or the service/cache layer

`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a second new device gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` at the store level. There is no test that an already-known device is still accepted (and updated) once the limit is reached, which is the main behaviour `updateDevice` exists for. There is also no test in `impl_test.go` that exercises `TagDevice` with a non-zero `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`, and no test of `Anonymous.Authenticate` returning an error for a rejected device; a service-level test issuing two requests from an over-limit device would have exposed the local-cache bypass described in another finding.

ErrDeviceLimitReached is a plain error, so rejected users get a generic unauthenticated response with no explanation

`ErrDeviceLimitReached` is defined with `fmt.Errorf` and is returned straight out of `Anonymous.Authenticate`. The authn/contexthandler layers only surface `errutil` errors with status codes and public messages; a plain error becomes a generic 401/redirect-to-login, and the authn service also logs a warning for every request from the rejected device. End users hitting the limit see a login page with no indication why anonymous access stopped working, and operators get noisy warn logs. Define it as an `errutil` error (e.g. `errutil.TooManyRequests`/`Unauthorized` with a public message) so the frontend can show a meaningful message, and consider lowering the log level for this expected condition.

New auth.anonymous.device_limit setting is not added to defaults.ini/sample.ini or the configuration docs

A new `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` key is read here, but the PR does not add it to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or `docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md`. Grafana's convention is that every setting appears in defaults.ini (so `grafana cli admin` / settings pages show it) and is documented, including the semantics of `0` meaning unlimited and what users experience when the limit is hit. Without this, operators have no discoverable way to learn the option exists or how it behaves.

ProvideAnonDBStore signature change is not reflected in the wire provider set

Before this change `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` received an `anonstore.AnonStore` via dependency injection, which means the server wire set had to contain a provider for it (`anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` plus a `wire.Bind(new(anonstore.AnonStore), new(*anonstore.AnonDBStore))`). This PR changes `ProvideAnonDBStore` to take an extra `deviceLimit int64` and constructs the store manually inside `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService`, but no change to `pkg/server/wire.go` is included. If the old provider/binding remains, `wire` generation fails (no provider for `int64`, and an unused `AnonStore` binding), breaking the build; if it is silently removed elsewhere, that change should be part of this PR so reviewers can verify it.

updateDevice mutates captured args inside a closure that WithDbSession may retry

`updateDevice` does `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` inside the callback passed to `WithDbSession`. `WithDbSession` re-invokes the callback on SQLite `locked`/`busy` errors (`retryOnLocks`), so on a retry the query string is prepended a second time and `dbSession.Exec(query, query, clientIP, ...)` is executed with one bind parameter too many, which fails and makes every retry attempt a guaranteed error. Build the full argument slice outside the closure (or inside it from a fresh slice) so retries are idempotent. The same pattern exists in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, but this PR introduces it anew in `updateDevice`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
enableSqlExpressions consults the feature flag but both branches return false (dead, inverted logic)

`enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the variable is true when the flag is *disabled*) and then returns `false` in both the `if enabled` branch and the fall-through. The flag lookup is therefore a no-op and the naming is inverted. If the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions (as the PR title says), the function should simply return false / the `case QueryTypeSQL` should return the error directly, with a comment referencing the CVE. As written, the code looks like a botched feature-flag gate, and a future maintainer is likely to 'fix' the inverted condition and silently re-enable the code path that led to CVE-2024-9264. Security-critical kill switches should not be expressed as misleading dead logic.

true_positives.golden_comment: The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

With `NewInMemoryDB()` now returning a stub whose `RunCommands` always errors, `TablesList` can never succeed, yet it still escapes the input, formats the DuckDB-specific `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` string, calls the stub, and then logs `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ..., "sql", rawSQL, "cmd", cmd)` on every invocation. Every attempt to use a SQL expression (including probes by attackers) now produces guaranteed Error-level log lines containing user-controlled SQL, and the surrounding `tablesFromAST`/`astError`/`existsInList` code is unreachable dead code. The variable is also still named `duckDB` even though the PR says it removes DuckDB references. The function should short-circuit with a clear 'disabled' error (or the whole file should be reduced to that) instead of going through an always-failing DuckDB-shaped path.

`NewSQLCommand` (used by the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`buildCMDNode` path as well as the new reader) now always fails because `sql.TablesList` calls the stubbed `RunCommands`, which unconditionally returns 'not implemented'. The failure is surfaced as `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", WithPublicMessage("error reading SQL command"))` and logged as `"invalid sql query"` at Warn level. This PR is the in-repo fix for a critical RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264), but it adds no tests. After this change the backend unconditionally rejects SQL expressions regardless of `FlagSqlExpressions`, but the flag is still registered in the feature registry with a description along the lines of 'Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions', is still listed in the feature-toggles documentation, and the frontend still exposes the SQL expression type when the flag is on. The PR description acknowledges leaving docs untouched, but at minimum the flag description and docs should state that the feature is disabled (and no longer DuckDB-based), or the flag should be marked as non-functional, so users are not misled into enabling a dead toggle.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

canManage() in V2 is granted by the VIEW scope on all-groups

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW or AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE on the all-groups ("Groups") resource: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. The interface Javadoc for canManage() was written to match this ("permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups"), so the mistake propagated to the contract as well. true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authz resource UUIDs instead of group IDs

In V2, group-specific authz resources are created with `name = group.getId()` (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveGroup), so the group ID is `groupResource.getName()`. This method instead passes `groupResource.getId()` (the Resource entity UUID) to hasPermission() and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result set. The result is consumed by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and by UsersResource.getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds) as a membership filter. Concretely: findByType(server, "Groups") returns the type-level "Groups" resource; hasPermission(<uuid>) cannot find a resource by that name and falls back to the all-groups resource, so an admin that has an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission gets `{<uuid of Groups resource>}` as its group filter. The user search then filters by membership in a non-existent group and returns zero users, and the count endpoint returns 0, even though canViewMembers() would grant access to every group member. The method needs to use the resource name for group resources and treat the type-level "Groups" resource separately (it is not a group ID).

false_positives.candidate:
Cleanup listener registration now depends on feature state at startup only

Previously the ProviderEventListener was always registered and `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` was evaluated per event. The change moves the check to registration time, so if the feature is enabled after the session factory has been initialized (the testing endpoint used by the legacy testsuite's `@EnableFeature(..., skipRestart = true)` does exactly this, and FeatureDeployerUtil does not re-run registerListener), the listener is never installed. Deleting a role, client or group then no longer calls management(...).setPermissionsEnabled(x, false), leaving orphaned authz Resource/Policy rows for the removed object. If this is intentional, the runtime feature-toggle path must re-register the listener.

Incorrect Javadoc on several GroupPermissionEvaluator methods

requireManageMembers(GroupModel) is documented as "Throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false", but the implementation (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) checks canManageMembers(GroupModel) — a different scope (manage-members vs manage-membership). canManage() (lines 72-78) is documented as granted by "permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups", which describes a view check and must not be the contract of a manage method. getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (line 145) says "@return Stream of IDs" but returns a Set<String>. Since these Javadocs are the only specification of the differing V1/V2 semantics, they should describe the intended behavior accurately.

Null resource from getResourceTypeResource is dereferenced

hasPermission() does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()`. getResourceTypeResource has three explicit `return null` paths (admin permissions not enabled on the realm, resource server is not the admin-permissions client, or the type-level resource is missing). realmResourceServer() only requires `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` to be non-null, so if the realm flag is turned off while the client still exists, or the session context realm differs from the realm being evaluated, every group permission check for a non-role admin ends in a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of a deny. Guard the null and return false.

Per-object resources are created without a type, so findByType("Groups") never finds group resources

getOrCreateResource creates the per-group (and per-user/per-client) Resource with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` and only updates scopes; it never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. Only the type-level resources created in init() get a type. Either set the type on created resources or do not rely on findByType in the V2 evaluator.

Tests do not exercise the paths that are broken in GroupPermissionsV2

The new test class never asserts a negative after granting an all-groups VIEW permission (testViewGroups grants VIEW on all groups and only checks listing), so the privilege escalation in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (VIEW grants group creation) goes undetected. There is no test with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permission followed by a user search or `users().count()`, which is the scenario where getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns resource UUIDs and the search returns no users. testManageGroupMembership (line 283) grants both the all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP and the group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission and only checks success; it never shows that the group-level permission is actually required (removing the group permission and expecting 403), so a no-op requireManageMembership would pass. Also missing: GET /groups/{id}/members with only VIEW_MEMBERS, and MANAGE_MEMBERS granting view of members. Please add these cases.

getResourceName maps resource names to human-readable values only for the USERS type ("All users" / username). The PR adds GROUPS but leaves this method unchanged, so for a group permission it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Group resources are created by getOrCreateResource without a display name (name = group ID, no displayName), so the API that lists the resources attached to a permission will return null names for group permissions, and the type-level "Groups" resource will not get an "All groups" label analogous to "All users". Add a GROUPS branch returning the group name/path (and a label for the type-level resource).

Federated recovery-code test covers only a single login; consumption, exhaustion and removal are untested

`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` sets up codes and performs one login with code #0. The companion test storage never marks a code as used (`isValid` is a plain `anyMatch` over all codes), always rebuilds the credential with all codes remaining, never exposes an id, and does not support `disableCredentialType`/`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` for this type. This method introduces a new, implicit contract for `CredentialInputUpdater` implementations: for type `recovery-authn-codes` the `CredentialInput.getChallengeResponse()` is a JSON-serialized array of plaintext codes, and `getCredentials(realm, user)` is expected to return a `CredentialModel` whose `credentialData`/`secretData` can be parsed by `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel` (otherwise `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` and the authenticator will throw). `createRecoveryCodesCredential` first calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`; if the user storage returns `true`, it logs and returns without touching Keycloak's own store. isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn-context processes, so hung flusher processes are never killed

In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the PR wraps `process.kill()` in `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Production flusher processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which yields `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess` directly and is NOT a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`), so the check is always False for real processes and `kill()` is never invoked. The previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally and worked. A slow-but-alive process will then flush the same shards concurrently with the new one (both can read the same expired segments from the Redis queue before `done_flush_segments` removes them, producing duplicate segments to Kafka), and up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS+1 processes can pile up per shard group. The same wrong check at line 346 in `join()` means `terminate()` is also never called on spawned processes (pre-existing, but this PR touched that code). Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Redis memory info is queried once per flusher process on every submit

`submit()` now iterates `self.buffers.values()` and calls `buffer.get_memory_info()` on each. `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info` reports cluster-wide node memory (it is not scoped to the buffer's assigned shards), so each of the N per-process buffers returns the same node list. The used/available ratio is unaffected (both sums scale by N), but the number of Redis INFO/MEMORY round trips per `submit()` now scales linearly with `--flusher-processes`, and with per-shard processes this can mean dozens of redundant cluster-wide queries per batch. Query memory info once (e.g. from a single buffer) rather than per process.

New multi-process flusher behaviour is only asserted structurally; no end-to-end or restart coverage

`test_flusher_processes_limit` only checks `len(flusher.processes) == 2` and that shard counts add up; it never submits spans to the different shards and verifies that each process's `SpansBuffer(shards)` actually flushes its own shards (and not others), nor that backpressure/health state is tracked per process. The restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` (which was rewritten and now contains the broken `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard) has no test at all, and both tests run with `produce_to_pipe` so only the thread code path is exercised, never real spawned processes or pickling of per-shard buffers.

Docstring claims one process per shard, but default is a single process

The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but the actual behaviour is `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` processes with shards round-robined across them, and the CLI option `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1, so production runs a single process unless configured otherwise. The `max_processes` parameter is also undocumented in the `:param:` list while `topic` (which does not exist) is documented. This will mislead operators about resource usage and about what `--flusher-processes` controls.

false_positives.candidate:
Old locally-stored recovery codes stay valid when new codes are accepted by the user storage

`createRecoveryCodesCredential` first calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)`; if the user storage returns `true`, it logs and returns without touching Keycloak's own store. Before this change recovery codes for federated (non-import) users were always written to Keycloak's federated-storage tables via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which also deletes any previously stored recovery-code credential. After upgrading, a federated user who already has such a local credential and regenerates codes will get the new set stored in the user storage while the old set remains in Keycloak DB. `UserCredentialManager.isValid` falls through to the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` when the storage rejects the input, so the old, supposedly replaced codes continue to authenticate the user, while the login page (driven by `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, which prefers the federated credential) asks for a number from the new set. The method should remove existing stored credentials of this type (e.g. via the credential provider's delete path) when the user storage accepted the new codes.

User label and generation timestamp are dropped on the user-storage path

The `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` passed in carries the user-chosen label (`userLabel` hidden field) and the `generatedAt` timestamp, but the `UserCredentialModel` handed to `updateCredential` only contains the type and the JSON list of raw codes. A user storage provider therefore has no way to persist the label or the real generation time (the test provider ends up with `userLabel == null` and `createdDate = now`). When the storage accepts the credential, the label the user typed is silently lost, which is a behavioral regression versus the local path where both are stored.

New user-storage SPI contract for recovery codes is undocumented and unverified

This method introduces a new, implicit contract for `CredentialInputUpdater` implementations: for type `recovery-authn-codes` the `CredentialInput.getChallengeResponse()` is a JSON-serialized array of plaintext codes, and `getCredentials(realm, user)` is expected to return a `CredentialModel` whose `credentialData`/`secretData` can be parsed by `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel` (otherwise `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` and the authenticator will throw). None of this is documented on the method, in `CredentialInputUpdater`, or in release notes. Additionally, unlike `createOTPCredential` which returns a boolean and validates the result, this method is `void` and trusts a `true` from `updateCredential` without any check, so a provider that answers `supportsCredentialType` liberally but does not persist the codes leaves the user with no recovery codes while the required action is marked complete.

Federated recovery-code test covers only a single login; consumption, exhaustion and removal are untested

`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` sets up codes and performs one login with code #0. The companion test storage never marks a code as used (`isValid` is a plain `anyMatch` over all codes), always rebuilds the credential with all codes remaining, never exposes an id, and does not support `disableCredentialType`/`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` for this type. Consequently the new production paths are not exercised for federated storage: that the next requested code number advances after use, the `allCodesUsed()` branch in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` (which now operates on a federated credential), re-generation replacing an older set, and removal via admin/account REST. A test that re-logs with a second code and asserts the requested code number, plus one exercising exhaustion, would catch the id/removal problem in the authenticator.

getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check

Every other method in this provider (`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`) guards against `getMyUser(user)` returning null, but `getCredentials` immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes`. `getCredentials` is reached via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` from the account REST endpoint and from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, so a `UserModel` adapter whose backing entry has been removed from the shared map (e.g. after `removeUser` in test cleanup while a session still holds the adapter) produces a `NullPointerException` instead of an empty stream.

The new test class never asserts a negative after granting an all-groups VIEW permission (testViewGroups grants VIEW on all groups and only checks listing), so the privilege escalation in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (VIEW grants group creation) goes undetected. `CreateOrUpdateDevice` reads `CountDevices(...)` and then, if `count < deviceLimit`, performs the upsert in a separate session. There is no transaction, lock, or conditional insert tying the two together, so N concurrent first-time devices (e.g. a burst of new visitors, or several Grafana instances each with an empty local cache) all observe `count < limit` and all insert, leaving the table above the limit. If the limit is intended as a hard cap (licensing/abuse control) this needs either a serialized check-and-insert (e.g. `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < ?` or the existing `serverlock`), or the docs should state that the limit is best-effort.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache is populated before the DB write, so a rejected device is let through on its next request

`tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` and only afterwards calls `anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. In practice the limit only blocks the first request; a page refresh bypasses it for ~29 minutes, after which the cycle repeats. The cache entry must only be set after a successful store write (or be removed on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`). This pattern was harmless before because tagging was best-effort, but it now defeats the feature.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies the exact same bug described in the golden comment: `tagDeviceUI` populates the local cache before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, meaning if `ErrDeviceLimitReached` occurs, the cached entry allows subsequent requests to bypass the limit for the 29-minute TTL.

`TagDevice` returns nil immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Authenticate` then grants the anonymous identity. Because the header is entirely client-controlled, any client (scripts, curl, a browser with the header stripped) can use anonymous access without ever being counted or limited, so the new `device_limit` setting cannot be relied upon to cap anonymous usage. Before this change `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` received an `anonstore.AnonStore` via dependency injection, which means the server wire set had to contain a provider for it (`anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` plus a `wire.Bind(new(anonstore.AnonStore), new(*anonstore.AnonDBStore))`). This PR changes `ProvideAnonDBStore` to take an extra `deviceLimit int64` and constructs the store manually inside `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService`, but no change to `pkg/server/wire.go` is included. If the old provider/binding remains, `wire` generation fails (no provider for `int64`, and an unused `AnonStore` binding), breaking the build; if it is silently removed elsewhere, that change should be part of this PR so reviewers can verify it.

updateDevice mutates captured args inside a closure that WithDbSession may retry

`updateDevice` does `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` inside the callback passed to `WithDbSession`. `WithDbSession` re-invokes the callback on SQLite `locked`/`busy` errors (`retryOnLocks`), so on a retry the query string is prepended a second time and `dbSession.Exec(query, query, clientIP, ...)` is executed with one bind parameter too many, which fails and makes every retry attempt a guaranteed error. `appStoreMetadata` (from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by the app's directory name (`googlecalendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`, ...), not by its slug (`google-calendar`, `zoom`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`). Indexing it with `app.slug` only works for apps whose dir name happens to equal the slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, zoho-bigin, webex). For the main apps this PR targets the lookup returns undefined and the endpoint responds 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug" even though the slug is correct, so credentials can never be synced for them. Use `getAppFromSlug(slug)` from `@calcom/app-store/utils` (or search `Object.values(appStoreMetadata)` by `slug`) instead.

Zoom refresh uses app identifier "zoomvideo" while the app slug (and webhook) use "zoom"

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the self-hoster's credential-sync endpoint, but the Zoom app's slug/appId everywhere else is `"zoom"` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` `appId: "zoom"`, and the inbound webhook resolves apps via `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug } })`). A self-hoster keying their endpoint by the slug they push through the webhook will not recognise `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token refresh fails in sync mode. Every other call site passes the real slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`, ...); this one should pass `"zoom"`.

Request to the credential-sync endpoint carries no authentication

The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as a form body, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other authentication material. The endpoint is expected to return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user ids, so the self-hoster has no way (short of network allow-listing) to verify the request originates from their Cal.com instance; anyone who can reach the endpoint can harvest every user's third-party tokens by enumerating ids. The PR already defines `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` for the inbound direction; the outbound request should at minimum send the same secret header so the endpoint can authenticate it.

Webhook secret compared with `!==` rather than a constant-time comparison

The secret header is validated with a plain string inequality against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. String comparison short-circuits on the first mismatching byte, which leaks timing information that can be used to recover the secret byte-by-byte on a network-reachable endpoint. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers (as other webhook handlers in the codebase do) and reject when lengths differ.

Several apps (e.g. Google Calendar) allow a user to hold multiple credentials for the same `appId`. The webhook selects `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no ordering and updates whichever row comes back, so a sync for one connected account can clobber the keys of a different connected account of the same provider. There is also no uniqueness constraint, so two concurrent webhook calls for a new user/app pair can both take the `create` branch and produce duplicate credentials. The payload should identify the target credential (or the provider account) rather than relying on `findFirst`.

The PR adds a new authenticated API route that writes third-party credentials into the DB and two shared helpers (`refreshOAuthTokens`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) that now sit in the token-refresh path of nine integrations, but ships no unit or integration tests (the PR description explicitly states tests were not added or run). Several of the defects in this change — the `[object Object]` schema key, the SafeParse wrapper being stored as the Google credential key, the missing `prisma` import in Salesforce, and the dirName-vs-slug lookup — would have been caught by even a minimal test exercising the webhook with a known slug and a test asserting the shape written to `prisma.credential.update` after a refresh.
